items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You played in both a small group and a big band situation with him. ... With Dizzy? Both. That is correct. In the big band situations I was playing in the trombone section...

ctx.x: Hootie Blues. Hootie Blues. I was in awe of that. It was just so wonderful to hear something, the likes of which you had never heard of in one play like that before. It's

true that during the final phases of my stay with Basie, I had become more and more curious about what was going on in New York City. Inevitably I left Basie’s band to settle down in New York – to live in New York and to learn as much as I could about what was going on in jazz and this so-called new approach to jazz that finally got the tag "bebop." As I understand it, Dizzy Gillespie created that word, "bebop." I think even recently I’ve said in print and in interviews that I’ve had some trouble with that term…
